Your business development team is working hard. But is everyone getting closer to their goals?

You see the meetings, introductions, and effort going into new opportunities. Understanding how that work translates into progress can be harder, especially when contributions take different forms.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit includes a Team Contribution & Goals dashboard: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

Supporting a business development team starts with understanding where people stand.

Some team members may be progressing steadily toward their goals, while others face challenges that deserve attention. Looking at attainment alongside credited contributions helps managers prepare more useful conversations.

Try reviewing each person's goal progress and recent contributions. Identify one achievement to recognize and one question worth asking before the next check-in.

People deserve more than a percentage beside their name in a performance report.

Goal attainment matters, but so do opportunity leadership, referrals, and supporting contributions. Those details can help explain how someone participates in the team's business development efforts.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit includes contribution reporting alongside individual goals: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

A performance conversation is more useful when you've looked beyond the headline results.

Comparing goals, credited value, and different contribution types can reveal questions worth exploring. It also gives managers a better foundation for discussing progress without overlooking the work behind it.

Try preparing your next team check-in with three notes for each person: goal progress, recent contributions, and one area where additional support might help.

Good leadership involves knowing when to recognize progress and when to offer support.

Business development reporting can help managers understand goal attainment, individual contributions, and the opportunities behind the results. That context makes performance conversations more thoughtful.

One of the harder parts of leading a business development team is balancing encouragement with meaningful accountability.

You want to recognize the effort people are making while understanding whether they're progressing toward their goals. Contribution reporting can provide useful context, but the conversations still matter.

For business development leaders, how do you recognize someone's hard work while discussing results that haven't met expectations?
